table.name: tbl_abundance_elements
table.remarks: Reference data specifying the type of element, part, or unit being counted, as represented by the values in tbl_abundances. For insects, this is usually the Minimum Number of Individuals (MNI) but can also refer to individual body parts like wings, shells, or leg segments. For plant remains (macrofossiles), it typically represents specific plant parts such as seeds, leaves, or bud scales.

column.name: element_name
column.remarks: Short name for element, e.g. mni, seed, leaf

column.name: element_description
column.remarks: Long description of element, e.g. minimum number of individuals, base of seed grain, covering of leaf or flower bud

table.name: tbl_abundance_ident_levels
table.remarks: Degree of certainty in taxonomic identification, such as at the Family, Genus, or Species level (e.g., cf. Family, cf. Genus, cf. Species).

table.name: tbl_abundance_modifications
table.remarks: Records modifications applied to individual counts, such as carbonized, corroded, or calcified specimens. This allows multiple instances of the same taxon to be recorded with different modifications (e.g., Hordeum sp. carbonized and Hordeum sp. unmodified).

table.name: tbl_abundances
table.remarks: Stores individual counts, presence data, or scaled values for biological proxies, linking an analysis entity to occurrences of a specific taxon. Essentially functions as a species list with counts for a single physical sample, with the intermediate analysis entity enabling multiple proxies per sample. Typically, it records count values (abundance) but may also indicate presence (1) or use categorical or relative scales, as defined by the data type within the dataset.

table.name: tbl_activity_types
table.remarks: Specifies the life stage or activity of an organism during a particular time of the year (e.g., adult, flowering).

column.name: activity_type
column.remarks: Activity type name

table.name: tbl_age_types
table.remarks: Frame of reference for denoting years (e.g. AD, BC, BP)

column.name: description
column.remarks: Description of frame of reference for denoting years (e.g. AD, BC, BP)

table.name: tbl_aggregate_order_types
table.remarks: 20120504pib: drop this? or replace with alternative?

column.name: description
column.remarks: explanation of ordering system

table.name: tbl_aggregate_samples
table.remarks: 20120504pib: can we drop aggregate sample name? seems excessive and unnecessary sample names can be traced.

table.name: tbl_alt_ref_types
table.remarks: What the sample name means (e.g. lab number, field number) Purpose or origin of the alternative sample reference/name. E.g. museum number, field sample number, on site excavation number

table.name: tbl_analysis_entities
table.remarks: An Analysis Entity allows the representation of multiple proxies for a single physical sample, essentially a virtual entity or statistical sample connecting physical samples to measurements or abundances (counts) for specific methods. Analysis entities are grouped by dataset, the construction of datasets are proxy dependent (see Dataset).

table.name: tbl_analysis_entity_ages
table.remarks: A virtual object defining a single proxy within a single physical sample, essentially a statistical sample. A single physical sample may have multiple analysis_entities each of which provide the linkages for the storage of different proxies. It also allows easier recording of specific species when used in (radiocarbon) dating.

table.name: tbl_analysis_entity_dimensions
table.remarks: Physical sample size used for analysis (often a subsample of physical sample) analysed sample non-analysed residue.

table.name: tbl_biblio
table.remarks: The centralized collection of bibliographic references within the SEAD database, storing detailed citations (author, title, year, publisher, DOI/URL) for sources like books and articles. It links to other domain-specific tables via foreign keys, allowing records to reference relevant literature. This setup ensures data integrity, credits sources, and supports research by organizing all bibliographic information in one place, thereby streamlining verification and study processes.

column.name: full_reference
column.remarks: The complete citation that details the source of information, data, or quotes used in a document, including the author, title, publication date, and publisher.

table.name: tbl_ceramics
table.remarks: Analysis results from ceramic thin-sections and sherds

table.name: tbl_chronologies
table.remarks: A cohesive collection of dated samples defined for a specific purpose, such as giving a single age range to each sample in a master dataset, or an age-depth model for a lake. Chornologies may be defined to simplify connection to external services which only allow for a limited scope of dating evidence to be included (e.g. GBIF, SBDI).

table.name: tbl_colours
table.remarks: Name and definition of colours according to specified method or colour space (e.g. Munsell, 2.5YR) .

table.name: tbl_contact_types
table.remarks: Name and description of the purpose of a contact (e.g. laboratory, sample taker, dataset creator).

table.name: tbl_contacts
table.remarks: Contact information for multiple purposes (e.g. dataset author, identifier of specimens, laboratory manager).

table.name: tbl_coordinate_method_dimensions
table.remarks: Support for which dimensions and their legal values for coordinate system methods. A list per coordinate system method with dimensions associated with that method. Additionally, the legal values (if any) of the given dimension can be specified.

table.name: tbl_data_type_groups
table.remarks: Grouping of different data types (e.g. relative scale, semi-quantitative)

table.name: tbl_data_types
table.remarks: Type of quantification used for the dataset, including classification system definitions.

table.name: tbl_dataset_contacts
table.remarks: One or more contacts for a dataset (e.g. data provider, digitaliser).

table.name: tbl_dataset_masters
table.remarks: Major grouping unit for datasets, usually designating contributing database, project, user or lab. E.g. BugsCEP, MAL, Lund Dendro lab

column.name: master_name
column.remarks: identification of master dataset, e.g. mal, bugscep, dendrolab

column.name: master_notes
column.remarks: description of master dataset, its form (e.g. database, lab) and any other relevant information for tracing it.

column.name: url
column.remarks: website or other url for master dataset, be it a project, lab or... other

table.name: tbl_dataset_submission_types
table.remarks: Lookup data listing types of dataset submission, e.g. original submission, ingestion from other database.

column.name: description
column.remarks: explanation of submission type, explaining clearly data ingestion mechanism

table.name: tbl_dataset_submissions
table.remarks: Records different submission events for a dataset (e.g. original recording to paper, entry into Bugs database, ingestion into SEAD).

column.name: notes
column.remarks: any details of submission not covered by submission_type information, such as name of source from which submission originates if not covered elsewhere in database, e.g. from bugscep

table.name: tbl_datasets
table.remarks: Datasets group collections of analysis_entities in a manner that is meaningful for the proxy concerned. For biological proxies, the dataset is usually equivalent of a spreadsheet containing samples and taxa for a single proxy. method of analysis (eg phosphates through citric acid extraction... etc)

column.name: dataset_name
column.remarks: something uniquely identifying the dataset for this site. may be same as sample group name, or created adhoc if necessary, but preferably with some meaning.

table.name: tbl_dating_labs
table.remarks: Radiocarbon laboratory identifiers and names from http://www.radiocarbon.org/Info/labcodes.html Allows transparency in C14 and other radiometric dating records.

column.name: contact_id
column.remarks: address details are stored in tbl_contacts

column.name: international_lab_id
column.remarks: international standard radiocarbon lab identifier. from http://www.radiocarbon.org/info/labcodes.html

table.name: tbl_dating_material
table.remarks: Details on material used for dating. Material may be either connected to a specific taxon (or pseudotaxon if at higher taxonomic level than species) or described in the material_dated text field. Specific abundance elements (e.g. seed, elytron) may also be selected. A date may consist of multiple dated materials.

table.name: tbl_dating_uncertainty
table.remarks: Lookup table listing possible forms of uncertainty for dates, such as "from", "to", "Ca." and "?". These are used either to establish ranges for ages (e.g. from mesolithic to neolithic; from AD100 to AD300)

table.name: tbl_dendro_dates
table.remarks: 20130722PIB: Added field dating_uncertainty_id to cater for >< etc. 20130722pib: prefixed fieldnames age_younger and age_older with "cal_" to conform with equivalent names in other tables

table.name: tbl_dimensions
table.remarks: Definition of different measurement types, such as sample weight, core length, according to a method group.

column.name: method_group_id
column.remarks: Limits choice of dimension by method group (e.g. size measurements, coordinate systems)

table.name: tbl_ecocode_definitions
table.remarks: Definition of ecological, habitat or ethnographic (etc) categories according to a defined system to which a taxon can be assigned.

table.name: tbl_ecocode_groups
table.remarks: Higher level grouping of taxon classifications allowing a single system to include multiple types of classification (e.g. Habitat, Food type, Food condition).

table.name: tbl_ecocode_systems
table.remarks: Definition of systems for classifying different aspects of taxa, such as habitat preference, food type, cultural use etc.

table.name: tbl_ecocodes
table.remarks: Maps classifications to individual taxa

table.name: tbl_feature_types
table.remarks: Archaeological feature types categorize features by their purpose, shape, or construction, aiding in the analysis of past human activities. Key types include domestic structures (homes), public and ceremonial spaces (temples, public buildings), economic/industrial areas (workshops, kilns), defensive structures (fortifications, walls), agricultural modifications (terraces, irrigation systems), funerary sites (graves, tombs), transportation routes (roads, bridges), and water management systems (wells, aqueducts). These classifications help understand societal organization, cultural practices, and technological advancements across different periods and locations.

table.name: tbl_features
table.remarks: An archaeological feature is a non-portable trace of past human activity, distinct from movable artifacts. Features include structures or alterations in the landscape indicating human behavior, such as building remains, hearths, burials, pits, roads, agricultural modifications like terraces, and defensive constructions like mounds and ditches. These elements are crucial for understanding ancient societies' spatial organization, cultural practices, and everyday life, providing context for interpreting artifacts and the environment. Archaeological features are studied in situ through excavation and surveying to glean insights into historical human-environment interactions.

column.name: feature_description
column.remarks: description of the feature. may include any field notes, lab notes or interpretation information useful for interpreting the sample data.

table.name: tbl_geochron_refs
table.remarks: References for geochronological (radiometric) dates for samples.

column.name: biblio_id
column.remarks: reference for specific date

table.name: tbl_geochronology
table.remarks: Radiometric dates for samples. Most are radiocarbon, but there are others (e.g. Uranium series). Also known as absolute dates.

column.name: error_older
column.remarks: plus (+) side of the measured error (set same as error_younger if standard +/- error)

column.name: error_younger
column.remarks: minus (-) side of the measured error (set same as error_younger if standard +/- error)

table.name: tbl_horizons
table.remarks: Technical name of the layer of soil the sample is from according to a defined standard (e.g. FAO A horizon)

table.name: tbl_identification_levels
table.remarks: Lookup data for taxonomic resolution/uncertainty in identification, and taxonomic level of uncertainty. e.g. c.f. Family, c.f. Genus, c.f. Species.

table.name: tbl_image_types
table.remarks: Metadata on the purpose or images (e.g. site photo, sample group sketch, core photo).

table.name: tbl_languages
table.remarks: Human language used for common name of taxa

table.name: tbl_lithology
table.remarks: Description of sediment units within a sample group. Allows for a soil profile to be described at depths in parallel to the sample depths (e.g. 0-10cm humus, 10-30cm sand).

table.name: tbl_location_types
table.remarks: Definitions of the resolution of geographical terms as well as there context (e.g. administrative unit, historical administrative unit, lake, country).

table.name: tbl_locations
table.remarks: Geographical location in physical (but sometimes historical) space. Usually defined in terms of regions.

column.name: default_lat_dd
column.remarks: default latitude in decimal degrees for location, e.g. mid point of country. leave empty if not known.

column.name: default_long_dd
column.remarks: default longitude in decimal degrees for location, e.g. mid point of country

table.name: tbl_mcr_names
table.remarks: The original taxon names used in the Birmingham MCR calculation system for climate reconstruction. Stored to enable reproducibility and cross-comparison with older results.

table.name: tbl_mcr_summary_data
table.remarks: Simple summaries of the maximum extent of the temperature tolerance of MCR species.

table.name: tbl_mcrdata_birmbeetledat
table.remarks: Definition of species climate enveolopes in binary 1 degree Celsius cells for TRange (columns) and TMax (rows). See www.bugscep.com for more info.

table.name: tbl_measured_value_dimensions
table.remarks: Stores eg. weight of samples used in measured value table, pre and post burning weights. But could also be volume or other dimension measures.

table.name: tbl_measured_values
table.remarks: A Measured value is a continues (non-discrete) chemical or physical (non-taxa) value of a certain dimension. A Sample Analysis can have (zero or) one measured values.

table.name: tbl_method_groups
table.remarks: Groups of (analysis) methods that have some form of similarity (e.g. dating methods, isotope analyses, palaeoentomology, geographical location).

table.name: tbl_methods
table.remarks: Definition of analysis methods.

table.name: tbl_modification_types
table.remarks: Allows the recording of multiple damage or change forms to the normal state of a (Quaternary/sub) fossil, such as carbonisation, mineralization, fragmentation etc.

table.name: tbl_physical_sample_features
table.remarks: Allow many-many between samples and specific (named) features, so that the same feature can have multiple samples, and one sample can come from a nested group of features or a feature with multiple names.

table.name: tbl_physical_samples
table.remarks: A Sample represents an instance of a material gathered at some point in time, at a specific Site, with a certain absolute or relative location (coordinate, depth etc) within that site, and within the context of a containing sample set. The physical qualities and properties of the sample, i.e. the various dimensions that describes the sample, are expressed via magnitudes of a specifc units (e.g. litre, kg etc.). The sample can also have additional (encoded) descriptive information, general notes and alternative external keys (in other ledgers or systems).

column.name: alt_ref_type_id
column.remarks: type of name represented by primary sample name, e.g. lab number, museum number etc.

column.name: sample_type_id
column.remarks: physical form of sample, e.g. bulk sample, kubienta subsample, core subsample, dendro core, dendro slice...

column.name: sample_name
column.remarks: reference number or name of sample. multiple references/names can be added as alternative references.

table.name: tbl_project_stages
table.remarks: Stages of investigation, e.g. desktop study, prospection, full excavation, reanalysis.

column.name: stage_name
column.remarks: stage of project in investigative cycle, e.g. desktop study, prospection, final excavation

table.name: tbl_project_types
table.remarks: Describes type of investigation in terms of main purpose/aim, e.g. teaching, consultanct, research, or combinations of these.

column.name: project_type_name
column.remarks: descriptive name for project type, e.g. consultancy, research, teaching; also combinations consultancy/teaching

column.name: description
column.remarks: project type combinations can be used where appropriate, e.g. teaching/research

table.name: tbl_projects
table.remarks: Name and description of project context for datasets for site(s).

column.name: project_abbrev_name
column.remarks: optional. abbreviation of project name or acronym (e.g. vgv, swedab)

column.name: description
column.remarks: brief description of project and any useful information for finding out more.

table.name: tbl_rdb
table.remarks: Rarety data for any taxon for a specified geographical area (e.g. threatenned in Sweden)

table.name: tbl_rdb_codes
table.remarks: Rarety data definitions according to different systems defined in tbl_rdb_systems

table.name: tbl_rdb_systems
table.remarks: Description of rarety designation systems (so called red data books) nad the region for which they are applicable

column.name: location_id
column.remarks: geaographical relevance of rdb code system, e.g. uk, international, new forest

table.name: tbl_record_types
table.remarks: Used to group biological proxies according to the way they are generally used, and/or their origin. It is used to provide useful subsets of the full taxonomic index, abundance_elements (i.e. so that "seed" is not an available option for insect data) and methods. Groups are made at the "Order" level in the taxonomic tree. E.g. "Insects & similar" groups insects with arthropods and other animals commonly extracted during insect work. "Plants & pollen" are grouped as they have similar ecological implications (i.e. presence of plant).

column.name: record_type_description
column.remarks: detailed description of group and explanation for grouping

table.name: tbl_relative_age_refs
table.remarks: Bibliographic information for the definition of a dating period (note: not the dating of a particular same, but an accepted authority for the date/age range).

table.name: tbl_relative_age_types
table.remarks: Relative age types, e.g. archaeological, Blytt-Sernander, Geological. Can be either quite precise in their definition (e.g. Blytt-Sernander) or generalising (e.g. Geological) as required.

table.name: tbl_relative_ages
table.remarks: Definitions of ages based on periods of calendar events. Includes age range and geographical relevance (e.g. Mesolithic Sweden)

column.name: relative_age_name
column.remarks: name of the dating period, e.g. bronze age. calendar ages should be given appropriate names such as ad 1492, 74 bc

column.name: description
column.remarks: a description of the (usually) period.

column.name: c14_age_older
column.remarks: c14 age of younger boundary of period (where relevant).

column.name: c14_age_younger
column.remarks: c14 age of later boundary of period (where relevant). leave blank for calendar ages.

column.name: cal_age_older
column.remarks: (approximate) age before present (1950) of earliest boundary of period. or if calendar age then the calendar age converted to bp.

column.name: abbreviation
column.remarks: Standard abbreviated form of name if available

table.name: tbl_relative_dates
table.remarks: Describes the relateive dating of aný sample by linking a relative age definition to a physical sample (via an analysis entity). Dates may include notes and indications of uncertainty (e.g. from, ca, <) as well as the method used for dating.

column.name: notes
column.remarks: any notes specific to the dating of this sample to this calendar or period based age

table.name: tbl_sample_alt_refs
table.remarks: Stores multiple names, of different types, for any physical sample (e.g. lab number = MAL01, field number = S1)

table.name: tbl_sample_coordinates
table.remarks: Physical location of sample, where available, as recorded on local grid or converted to other standard. Uses methods table to look up type of grid, which enables all samples recorded with Lat/Long to be easily plotted on large scale maps, but local grids to be plotted on a site/project basis.

column.name: accuracy
column.remarks: GPS type accuracy, e.g. 5m 10m 0.01m

table.name: tbl_sample_description_types
table.remarks: Definitions of types for sample descriptions

table.name: tbl_sample_descriptions
table.remarks: Descriptions of samples according to different description types

table.name: tbl_sample_dimensions
table.remarks: Measurable dimension type data for samples, excluding coordinates, but including depth or sample in stratigraphy or core. E.g. size of sample on arrival (volume, weight etc), depth of sample top, depth of sample bottom. Note that the name and description of the dimension are stored in tbl_dimension.

column.name: dimension_id
column.remarks: details of the dimension measured

table.name: tbl_sample_group_coordinates
table.remarks: Coordinates for sample groups. E.g. top of core, top of profile dendrochronological object, ceramic object.

table.name: tbl_sample_group_description_type_sampling_contexts
table.remarks: Groups description types to methods. For dendro, a bunch of description types at different levels of detail. This then groups those types and says: These fields groups things from a dendro building?

table.name: tbl_sample_group_description_types
table.remarks: Defines the type of a description for a sample group. Definition types include building structure data information (roof, structure type, etc) or dendro annotation data surrounding wrecks. These descriptions should not be used to determine sampled features. They are defined for samples. User added lookup data.

table.name: tbl_sample_group_descriptions
table.remarks: Description or definition of a group of samples according to a sample group description type

table.name: tbl_sample_group_dimensions
table.remarks: Physical dimensions of a sample group (e.g. core length) according to a defined dimension type

table.name: tbl_sample_group_images
table.remarks: Images of the sample group (e.g. a photograph or annotated sketch of a core)

table.name: tbl_sample_group_notes
table.remarks: Notes on the group of samples

table.name: tbl_sample_group_references
table.remarks: Bibliographic information that is specific or most relevant for the sample group and not the site or dataset (e.g. a paper reinterpreting one structure from a site)

table.name: tbl_sample_group_sampling_contexts
table.remarks: Type of situation under which the sample group was collected, investigation purpose, or other initial collection purpose. E.g. stratigraphic sequence, invertebrate survey, archaeological excavation, Quantitative vegetation survey. It provides a collection context for the sample group and provides for extraction/analysis on only samples collected in a specific type of project. For example, climate reconstruction using only strategraphic sequences, habitat analysis using only modern survey data.

column.name: description
column.remarks: full explanation of the grouping term

column.name: sort_order
column.remarks: allows lists to group similar or associated group context close to each other, e.g. modern investigations together, palaeo investigations together

table.name: tbl_sample_groups
table.remarks: A collection of related samples. Common groups are all samples from a structure (e.g. House 1), a stratigraphic sequence (e.g. profile 3) or a lake core, but groups may be defined in any way.

column.name: method_id
column.remarks: sampling method, e.g. russian auger core, pitfall traps. note different from context in that it is specific to method of sample retrieval and not type of investigation.

table.name: tbl_sample_horizons
table.remarks: Technical soil layer to from which the sample was taken.

table.name: tbl_sample_images
table.remarks: Images of samples (e.g. photograph from the site, lab processing, microscope images)

table.name: tbl_sample_locations
table.remarks: Description of the sample's location according to defined types

table.name: tbl_sample_notes
table.remarks: General notes on the sample that do not fit in other tables (e.g. stored in a cellar until processing in 2020).

column.name: note_type
column.remarks: origin of the note, e.g. field note, lab note

column.name: note
column.remarks: note contents

table.name: tbl_sample_types
table.remarks: Physical form of the sample. Normally these will either be subsamples relating the sample group sampling method, or bulk samples. e.g. Core subsample, grab sample, bulk (bag) sample

table.name: tbl_season_types
table.remarks: Defines the grouping of seasons.

table.name: tbl_seasons
table.remarks: Contains names of seasons and months for use in describing activities.

table.name: tbl_site_images
table.remarks: Images at the site level (e.g. site photograph, aerial photograph, location map).

table.name: tbl_site_locations
table.remarks: ?Connects sites and location names?

table.name: tbl_site_natgridrefs
table.remarks: General site coordinates using national grid system, e.g. UK Ordinanace Survey National Grid, Swedish SWEREF99. A site can be defined on multiple grids (e.g. Swedish RT90 and SWEREF99TM)

table.name: tbl_site_other_records
table.remarks: Information on the availability of data not currently stored in SEAD. One record should be used for each proxy type even if they refer to the same publication. Note that some of these data may be entered into SEAD at a later date. Submission requests may be made to the SEAD project group.

column.name: biblio_id
column.remarks: reference to publication containing data

column.name: record_type_id
column.remarks: reference to type of data (proxy)

table.name: tbl_site_preservation_status
table.remarks: Information on preservation level of sites and risks to cultural heritage. One record per preservation status/threat. Table added at request of PAN (Polar Archaeology Network) members and is aimed at providing support for evaluation of threats to (Arctic) cultural heritage.

column.name: description
column.remarks: brief description of site preservation status or threat to site preservation. include data here that does not fit in the other fields (for now - we may expand these features later if demand exists)

table.name: tbl_site_references
table.remarks: Allows listing of publications at site level. Note that publications refering to only a set of sample_groups or physical_samples or specific dataset etc are stored at the appropriate lower level in the hierarchy.

table.name: tbl_sites
table.remarks: A Site in SEAD refers to a single Location excavated or sampled for the purpose of building environmental pre- and historical data records. The Samples are grouped into Sample Sets.

column.name: site_location_accuracy
column.remarks: Accuracy of highest location resolution level. E.g. Nearest settlement, lake, bog, ancient monument, approximate

table.name: tbl_species_association_types
table.remarks: List of permissable associations between species, e.g. predates on; is predated by; parasitic on; parasitized by etc.

table.name: tbl_species_associations
table.remarks: Describes the relationship of one taxon to others, such as predation, paracitism, common habitat etc. Also includes synonym links. Note that the direction of the association is important in most cases (e.g. x predates on y)

table.name: tbl_taxa_common_names
table.remarks: Vernacular (=common) name of an organism (e.g. bluebottle)

table.name: tbl_taxa_images
table.remarks: Stores links to images of taxa either stored in another database or online.

table.name: tbl_taxa_measured_attributes
table.remarks: Any size related measurement of an organism (e.g. max length)

table.name: tbl_taxa_reference_specimens
table.remarks: Information on reference and type specimens used for primary description of species.

table.name: tbl_taxa_seasonality
table.remarks: Stores the part of the year (e.g. Winter, June) in which a particular activity or developmental stage occurs (e.g. adult June-August).

column.name: location_id
column.remarks: geographical relevance of seasonality data

table.name: tbl_taxa_synonyms
table.remarks: Alternative scientific names of taxa, including primary reference for definition or use.

column.name: synonym
column.remarks: Synonym at level defined by id level. I.e. if synonym is at genus level, then only the genus synonym is included here. Another synonym record is used for the species level synonym for the same taxon only if the name is different to that used in the master list.

table.name: tbl_taxa_tree_authors
table.remarks: Authority for the species name or synonym

table.name: tbl_taxa_tree_families
table.remarks: Taxonomic family

table.name: tbl_taxa_tree_genera
table.remarks: Taxonomic genera

table.name: tbl_taxa_tree_master
table.remarks: Finest level of taxonomic identity, usually species, but may be sp. for unknown single species, spp. for unknown multiple species, grp for taxnomic group, or split identifications (x/y) or a number of other cases depending on taxonomic group.

table.name: tbl_taxa_tree_orders
table.remarks: Taxonomic order level in the hierarchy

table.name: tbl_taxonomic_order
table.remarks: Taxonomic code which allows ordered placement in a taxonomic ordering system (checklist) or reference to another database system (e.g. GBIF, Artdatabanken)

table.name: tbl_taxonomic_order_biblio
table.remarks: Bibliographic information for the taxonomic ordering or numbering system (may be multiple references)

table.name: tbl_taxonomic_order_systems
table.remarks: Systems for ordering or numbering taxa systematically so as to allow for a unique and name independent identifier for any taxon. It also allows mapping between different systems to enable connectivity between databases.

table.name: tbl_taxonomy_notes
table.remarks: General notes on a taxon, usually on identification (e.g. easily confused with x) with references, but amy also indlude links to images.

table.name: tbl_tephra_dates
table.remarks: Sample dates based on tephrachronology, including uncertainty (e.g. >) and notes.

table.name: tbl_tephra_refs
table.remarks: Bibliographic data for tephra (volcanic ash layer) definitions.

table.name: tbl_tephras
table.remarks: Definitions of volcanic as layers and their age ranges (e.g. Hekla 1984).

table.name: tbl_text_biology
table.remarks: Ecological, habitat and behavioural information for taxa, including reference for the source. E.g. in hollows on old oaks.

table.name: tbl_text_distribution
table.remarks: Text based distribution information for taxa, including reference for the source. E.g. Scandinavia north of Tromso, Bitish Isle - rare.

table.name: tbl_text_identification_keys
table.remarks: Identification key extracts with bibliographic source.

table.name: view_taxa_alphabetically
table.viewSql: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_name AS "order", f.family_id, f.family_name AS family, g.genus_id, g.genus_name AS genus, s.taxon_id, s.species, a.author_id, a.author_name AS author FROM ((((tbl_taxa_tree_master s JOIN tbl_taxa_tree_genera g ON ((s.genus_id = g.genus_id))) JOIN tbl_taxa_tree_families f ON ((g.family_id = f.family_id))) JOIN tbl_taxa_tree_orders o ON ((f.order_id = o.order_id))) LEFT JOIN tbl_taxa_tree_authors a ON ((s.author_id = a.author_id))) ORDER BY o.order_name, f.family_name, g.genus_name, s.species;
